notes: organic mantle during phase A: Tanisha -> Rosa d13

convoLines.text: "Can we talk?" Imani shifts their weight. "I need something to do. Anything. Please."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
You walk to the cache spot with Imani. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Tanisha always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I trust you? I mean really."
"That's the right answer. The wrong one would've been 'yes' too fast. How are you holding up, though?"
"Still on whether they can trust you. Good talking."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I dreamed Tanisha was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Tanisha said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Nobody says Tanisha's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"This cut — I can't clean it properly one-handed. Will you help me clean it?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Tanisha owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Sleep's gone strange. I wake before anyone else at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About this wound — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Last time things were different. They always are." "The whole fire was arguing about The Anaconda Empress last night — what to even CALL it. 'Big Big' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"The fire'll settle it. It settles everything, eventually."
"My vote? I'm keeping it to myself until the shouting stops."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
You said you'd earn it, not that I should just hand it over. Fair. I'm watching — and so far, so good.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Purslane — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
You spend time tending them. This was care, not a promise of a cure.
"Alright, love. Go do what you need to do."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Leroy sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
Leroy has an edge today — something curdled.
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the ridge above the creek."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the ridge above the creek — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Cooking With Teeth. They just... took Carlos. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
"Still on what's been happening. That's still where we are."
"What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About this wound — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took Carlos — Cooking With Teeth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
You walk to the hollow with Imani. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said there was something you regretted. You didn't want to get into it. I won't ask. Just — are you carrying it any lighter?"
They nod. "Okay."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Can I be honest? Still on that personal stuff."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
Leroy has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Duel. They just... took Wanjiru. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Imani: "You. Yeah, you. What do you make of this?"
"Take your time."
"What's this about? Where are you from — originally? Before all this."
Nods slowly. "Columbus, Ohio. I'll remember that. Everybody's from somewhere that isn't here."
"Still on where you're from."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that favor."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Sassafras — I keep thinking about what you said. I'm seeing it everywhere now."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that plant lesson."
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the creek bend, past the treeline."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the creek bend, past the treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
As I said — Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that favor."
"This was good." They mean it.
You told me you're from Columbus, Ohio. Do you think about it much?
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that personal stuff."
A pause. When they speak again, it's about something else entirely.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"We're eating through stores faster than we replace them. Forage with me tomorrow? I know the south slope below the meadow."
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the south slope below the meadow in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Anyway — I should get going."
"No — you're right, it's a lot. Forget it."
"This was good." They mean it.

deathBeat: d13: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Tanisha Jackson is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d13: 🕯️ Tanisha Jackson is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d14: That night, they bring Tanisha home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d13: SYSTEM: "Perimeter violated! This is unprecedented! ...Is this unprecedented? Checking. Yes. Unprecedented."
d13: SYSTEM: "INTRUDER REPELLED. The pantry’s aroma is now classified as a defensive liability. The audience is chanting the defenders’ names. Fan clubs are forming. This is how it starts."
d13: SYSTEM: Quest protocol integrated. Objectives will appear.
d13: SYSTEM: Catalogued. The Codex grows teeth.

d14: ◈ ARC III — ENGINES. SYSTEM: "VIEWERSHIP MILESTONE. Organic unit demonstrates compounding capability. Resonance protocols unlocked." — Your gifts deepen. Used in sequence, they resonate. The village is no longer just surviving. It is becoming something.
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "AUDIENCE EXPANSION! Your party cap is now FOUR! The people demanded bigger ensembles! Don't let us down!"
d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "A viewer sent this. A FAN. We checked. It is not dinner." A pause. "We checked twice. The fans are very insistent that you open it ON CAMERA."
burialWindowSay: d14: That night, they bring Tanisha home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d16: You say a few words for Tanisha. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d16: You bury Tanisha. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d16: "Tanisha always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d16: "You want to know about that? Okay." "I dreamed Tanisha was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
d16: "I keep turning over the last thing Tanisha said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d16: "Nobody says Tanisha's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
d16: "Tanisha owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
echoV2Sample: d16: The village raises a marker by the fire — Tanisha, day 16. the wild. A place to stand.
